## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Varuṇajātaka* (Ja 71) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. In its frame narrative (the "story of the present," *paccuppannavatthu*), set at Jetavana near Sāvatthi, the Buddha delivers the teaching in connection with the Elder Tissa, the Squire's Son [SuttaCentral]. The introductory story recounts how thirty young men of Sāvatthi ordained, completed their initial five-year training under their preceptors, and subsequently requested a meditation subject (*kammaṭṭhāna*) chosen by the Buddha from among thirty-eight meditation themes before departing to embrace the forest-dwelling ascetic life [SuttaCentral; Shaw 2006]. Modern scholarship notes that this story of the present reflects later commentary-layer developments distinct from the canonical verses [Shaw 2006].
Regarding parallels and textual reuse, SuttaCentral lists resembling parallels in the Theragāthā, specifically the *Bākulattheragāthā* (Thag 3.3) and the *Hāritattheragāthā* (Thag 3.15) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus detects no internal Pali text reuse and no cross-language alignments with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora meeting the threshold score [DharmaNexus].
